claim: Clinicians neglect base rates when interpreting a positive test; the error is stable (18% correct in 1978, 23% in 2013, N=60/61; modal answer 95% vs true about 2%).
agent_test: Give the agent the Casscells problem and a prose variant; compare mental posterior vs code posterior at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Practitioners overestimate pretest and post-test probability in written vignettes (N=553); error size varies by test (stress test positive LR 21 vs 2.0-2.7; urine culture matched).
agent_test: Replicate vignettes on the agent with and without an LR table in code.

claim: The Pauker-Kassirer two-threshold rule (testing threshold, test-treatment threshold) says test only when belief lies between thresholds.
agent_test: Compute thresholds in code; compare always-test vs threshold-gated S7 on tokens and accuracy.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Thresholds are not fixed facts; they move with regret, cost of error and intuitive weightings.
agent_test: Vary the stated cost of a wrong answer and check that test-or-stop behaviour shifts as the rule predicts.

claim: Natural frequencies raise correct Bayesian answers (4% to 24% pooled; 10% to 46% in physicians), but most people still fail.
agent_test: Compare probability vs count format in the prompt; expect a smaller effect than in humans; code arithmetic should dominate both.

claim: Frequency benefit is moderated by visuals, brevity, numeracy, training and prior exposure; for two chained tests odds/LR beat frequencies (10.6% vs 4.9%).
agent_test: Test chained-test problems in odds+LR form vs counts, with and without code.

claim: Two theories explain the frequency effect (ecological rationality vs nested sets); no decisive result.
agent_test: None needed; a design choice only.

claim: LLMs follow Bayes when all numbers are supplied but use similarity and ignore base rates when priors or diagnosticity must be recalled.
agent_test: Ask for prior and likelihoods as separate fields and compute the posterior in code vs one-shot posterior.

claim: LLM probability estimates are unreliable: GPT-4 beats clinicians on pretest and post-negative but fails the positive stress test (69% vs 2-11%); o1-preview fixes that one case only.
agent_test: Supply a retrieved LR table; compare error against recalled numbers.

claim: Label framing drives LLM error: bacteriuria framed as UTI gave 26% pretest vs 0-1% truth.
agent_test: Test mismatched-label vignettes; add a check that the named disease matches the finding.

claim: ChatGPT writes Bayes correctly with abstract letters (19/20) but drops the covariate with medical names (50-60% error); a stepwise prompt removes conditioning errors.
agent_test: Prompt abstract-symbol setup then substitute; code the arithmetic.

claim: Asking an LLM directly for a pretest probability from records is near chance (AUROC about 50) though embeddings carry signal.
agent_test: Do not use verbalised priors; use a table or counts.

claim: LLMs do not accumulate belief over rounds; prompting fixes did not help, fine-tuning did.
agent_test: Keep belief state in code across steps; compare to model-held belief at equal tokens.

claim: Selecting questions or tests by expected information gain with a stop rule beats direct prompting by large margins (UoT +38.1%, BED-LLM +37.4 points), but against a strong halving/best-split heuristic at equal tokens the gain is small on medical diagnosis (UoT 88.4 vs 85.1 at 4.6k tokens; 92.5 vs 86.7 at 9k) and variable on 20 Questions (BED-LLM over Split about +2 to +28 points). Outcomes are LLM-simulated and uncalibrated; ACTMED about 50% fewer tests.
agent_test: Implement EIG test choice in code with a stop rule; compare with LLM-chosen tests.

claim: A scaffold with Bayesian differential, discriminating tests and cost stewardship lifted sequential diagnosis (preprint: 79.9% at $2,396 vs o3 78.6% at $7,850; no-budget 81.9% at $4,735; Science 2026: 83.2% NEJM, 80.3% MIMIC-IV-ED vs physicians 36.1/46.8). The test-chooser role was never ablated alone; debate and cost tracking are bundled.
agent_test: Ablate the test-chooser role alone.

claim: Naive interactive questioning can hurt LLMs (-11.3% relative); confidence-gated asking helps.
agent_test: Gate test requests on confidence or EIG.

claim: Corpus co-occurrence priors are a cheap second signal; agreement of unlike methods raises accuracy (64.7% vs about 47%).
agent_test: Cross-check the LLM answer against a count-based prior.

claim: Giving physicians GPT-4 did not improve diagnosis (76% vs 74%); the LLM alone scored higher.
agent_test: Context only.

claim: Asked for likelihood ratios, GPT-4o/o3/GPT-5 are unbiased on average (0.99-1.02x) but single values are several-fold off (95% limits 0.26x-3.70x for GPT-5; 0.23x-4.53x GPT-4o) and shrink toward 1 (calibration slope 0.73-0.88); lab-test LRs are worst. Memorisation not excluded.
agent_test: Elicit LR as a range; compare with table LRs; flag lab tests.

claim: Published test accuracy is inflated by weak design and is not portable: case-control design gives diagnostic odds ratios about 3.0x higher (CI 2.0-4.5); sensitivity or specificity shifts 0-40 points across prevalence within a review (significant in 8 of 23); a single pooled value overstated detected positives by 10.8-19.1% in community settings.
agent_test: Store LRs as ranges with setting and design flags; check whether a decision flips across the range.

claim: Chaining LRs under an independence assumption overstates the posterior when tests share a hidden driver; in a toy case (Se=Sp=0.9, prior 0.1, both positive) 0.90 falls to 0.50-0.70 with plausible shared false-positive covariance. Dependence cannot be learned from small data (identifiable only with 4+ tests or a strong prior). No LLM or human chaining study found.
agent_test: Group tests that share a mechanism; cap combined LR; widen interval after chaining; test on agent.

claim: Without stated costs, LLMs over-order: GPT-3.5-turbo recommended radiology with sensitivity 0.96-0.98 and specificity 0.13-0.23 across four prompts; 'only if absolutely required' barely helped. Exam-recommendation precision of reasoning LLMs is 23-42% against the real workup. No study tests the Pauker-Kassirer thresholds directly.
agent_test: Compute test/test-treat thresholds in code from stated costs; count tests that cannot change the action.

claim: More free turns do not improve test choice: recall of needed tests stayed 37-44% and fell for some models, accuracy rose only 2-5 points, models looped on repeated requests; stopping behaviour depends strongly on case mix and protocol, so stop-rule comparisons need a fixed simulator and turn cap. No head-to-head of stop rules found.
agent_test: Add a loop guard and compare posterior-margin vs information-gain-floor stops with the simulator fixed.

claim: LLMs do not adopt natural frequencies by default and misapply them when told to (3 models, one problem family); on textbook counts problems they appear far above human norms (indirect). No controlled LLM test of counts vs probability format found.
agent_test: Test counts vs probabilities on novel-number problems; build counts in code.

claim: Separating factor elicitation from the arithmetic (LLM proposes factors and coarse support; a Bayesian model computes) beats verbalised LLM probabilities (F1 59%, more than 30% above GPT-4) and matches or beats CoT on decisions with Llama-2/3.1. Not shown for diagnosis, frontier models or equal tokens.
agent_test: Run elicit-then-compute vs one-shot posterior at equal tokens.

claim: Stated confidence of 2025 models can be uninformative: Gemini 2.5 Pro confidence 9.66 correct vs 9.67 incorrect; ChatGPT-5 9.42 vs 7.80 (p=0.04). No recalibration of pretest probability on the Morgan vignettes for current models found.
agent_test: Do not gate on verbalised confidence alone.
